Before reaching for it, ask whether you need parallelism at all. Putting

in front of each call on one context is correct and usually fast enough: async already frees the thread while each query waits. Parallel contexts pay off only when queries are slow and truly independent, and they cost something. Each one borrows its own pooled connection, so one request holds three at once, and the queries share no transaction, so they can see the database at slightly different moments.
